assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original EED medieval forest-village quest-space pixel-art review board, two equal independent panels, not city overview. Reference only restrained green forest, weathered brown wood, simple thatch, earthy paths and grey stones. Coarse crisp low-detail pixel clusters; top-down oblique ORTHOGRAPHIC game camera, horizontal beams, vertical posts, axis-aligned square floor tiles where paved, no diamond isometric. LEFT EED-D01-A old-beam grain inspection shed. ONE detached old timber sample lies securely on two low trestles with worm holes, short/long cut notches on its side; two plain payment tally tokens separated on small side table. A manual frame saw hangs safely against BACK wall, outside visitor access; no sawing underway. Open front and clear wide bypass around sample, no timber falling over entrance. Backdrop occupied home remains intact with supporting roof beams untouched; no empty evacuated home or fresh deforestation. RIGHT EED-D01-B worker quotation pavilion, facing public village lane with forest behind. Three separate simple blank wooden quote tablets on table, each physically spaced; plain single-batch wooden permission peg beside closed folio, no common grand permit or authority seal. No people, readable words, numbers, sale completed or removal of house beams. Modest sparse furnishings, no giant lumber stock, no national headquarters, no bed. Two separate unobstructed street openings. Neutral dry daylight, muted olive and umber, clear silhouettes, no watermark.
assets.qa: Detached worm-marked sample on two trestles, safely stored frame saw, intact background home and three separate blank quote tablets appear. Front bypass visually clear; extra stacked planks are decorative rather than approved stock. No live house beam removal, transaction or nationwide permit depicted. High-resolution review style, pixel grid/collision not validated.

assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original forest village paired quest-space pixel-art review board. Two equal panels. Only use reference for timber-thatch, subdued olive woods and earth-stone palette; no whole-city duplication. Coarse crisp pixels with simple readable silhouettes, orthographic top-down-oblique, horizontal wall lines, vertical posts, square-axis paths not isometric diamonds. LEFT EED-D02-A public forest-edge tree-section inspection pavilion: fixed OLD detached cross-section disk on low sturdy table showing dark damaged core, beside a small intact comparison sliver. In BACK CORNER ONE still-standing tree with localized dark bark damage is fenced securely, no felled trunk, no saw or axe in action; nearby healthy trees unmarked. Plain old boundary notch on one low stone. Clear public bypass does not enter fenced tree zone or any home. No claim all forest diseased or newly healed. RIGHT EED-D02-B small patrol shift-change hut opening directly onto same public village path, plain wooden whistle on counter, three anonymous patrol-route tally pegs and one CLOSED shift folio. Wall board contains only short abstract route strokes, NO maps to homes, names or addresses. No beds, debt documents, national insignia or military command center. Two broad independent doorway gaps to path, no lock on return, no people, no speech or musical symbols. Neutral daylight, natural nonmagical materials. No words/numbers/labels or watermark.
assets.qa: Old damaged cross-section and comparison slice, fenced standing damaged tree, public bypass and anonymous shift hut rendered. Whistle, three pegs and closed folio are visible; route board includes generic trees/hills but no houses or addresses. Disease extent and fencing safety not established by image. No felling, cure or new patrol staffing claimed.

assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Two paired original forest-village riverbank quest spaces, pixel-art REVIEW board. Reference only muted olive woodland, weathered wood, thatch, earth-grey bank stone. Coarse readable crisp pixels, orthographic top-down oblique with horizontal shore and vertical posts, axis-aligned square paving, no diamond isometric. LEFT EED-D03-A small raft waterline weighing shelter at LOW river bank. One modest tightly moored timber raft on calm water with a few old detached beams tied in place, visible immersion marks on mooring post, fixed rounded stone weight on low dry shelf under a tiny roof. It is a load-study prop, no claimed carrying capacity. Continuous HIGH embankment public footpath runs behind shore with protective edge rail and remains independent of low loading steps. RIGHT EED-D03-B detached authorized-beam storage lean-to on dry higher bank: just two old salvaged beams with exposed end joints on low rack, separate blank refund token on little counter, no loading or dismantling happening. Behind, intact small occupied-style house with roof fully supported and closed private door; no roof holes, no missing live structural beams, no evacuation evidence. Broad independent open route from shelter to high embankment path, no bridge built from house. No people, text, numbers, magical effects, industrial crane, huge inventory or completed refund. Natural earth, brown and slate palette, daylight, no watermark.
assets.qa: Moored modest raft at low bank and continuous higher path are visible, with stone weight and detached storage beams beside intact house. Waterline marks subtle and exact load capacity absent; raft appears mainly unloaded and stone is on ground rather than shelf. No residence dismantled or completed refund. Heights, rail safety and collision are review-only.
